# Promotional application and resumed-runtime progress boundaries

Keep the original LuT318 failed report. Its late native freeze differed by 0.806–0.845 m for six patrolling hornlings after heavyblade adoption. Closed-profile read-only Core records prove that all eight old components and the player were unchanged in previous_world, migration input and the actual candidate-save application output. No source, pose, database or production code was edited to obtain this evidence.

The six-stage native fixture retains raw live snapshots, timestamps, frame observations and actual gameplay probes. After normal shutdown, match each unique applied application by world/candidate/build, require successful native launch evidence, exact input/output migration identity, and strict equality of every old component field, player and existing world progress. Added component IDs are permitted. A pose reset must fail even if input and output both repeat the reset.

Cold verification separates exact closed-Core persistence from a later native snapshot. Keep the full native comparison result and raw snapshots. With actual nonzero scene physics counters, explicitly mark these source-driven values unconfirmed: hornling position/yaw, player position/onFloor, idle heavyblade stamina/staminaDelay/dodgeCooldown/invulnerable, and rifle cooldown/reloadRemaining. All other persistent values remain exact, including health, IDs, config, equipment and inventory. Unknown/missing frame evidence or unlisted changes are failures. No numeric pose tolerance is used and no complete zero-frame native restore claim is made.

Run tests/direct-library-application-audit.test.mjs and tests/direct-library-promo-scenario.test.mjs without GPU. The frozen real receipt fixture must pass strict application preservation and still expose the original later-live mismatch; injected position/yaw/health/player resets must fail. The coordinating owner performs the separate sealed native rerun. Keep modelCalls=0 for this local library test; it is not a DeepSeek behavior measurement.
